sections.title: Bereishit and the Three Foundations of Creation
sections.summary: The opening word of the Torah contains creation and points toward reverence, the covenant, and Shabbat.

sections.title: Five Lights, Six Gifts, and the Oral Torah

sections.title: Tishrei, Nisan, and the Path to Redemption
sections.summary: The two traditions concerning creation and redemption illuminate repentance, Torah, and the cycle of the year.

sections.title: The Shabbat Meals and the Divine Presence
sections.summary: The language of the holy meals expresses the distinct spiritual illuminations of Shabbat and Yom Tov.

topics.h: The Distinct Mysteries of the Shabbat Meals

sections.title: The Hidden Light and the Protection of Shabbat
sections.summary: The primordial light, the Tree of Knowledge, and the guarding of Shabbat reveal the struggle to separate good from evil.

For the righteous—"and your people are all righteous"—

sections.title: Adam’s Teshuvah and the Redemptive Power of Shabbat
sections.summary: The aftermath of Eden is understood through repentance, the serpent’s influence, and the higher and lower Shabbat.

sections.title: Shabbat as Hashem’s Gift of Sanctification

sections.title: The Gift of Rest and the Inner Holiness of Shabbat
sections.summary: Shabbat rest is more than cessation from work: it is a revelation of divine holiness within Israel.

sections.title: Passing Through Waters and Fire with Hashem
sections.summary: The promise of divine accompaniment illuminates the passage from fear and spiritual danger toward protection.

sections.title: The Patriarchs and the Gathering of Israel
sections.summary: The three patriarchal attributes and the three Shabbat meals point toward the unification of Israel.

sections.title: Transforming Bitterness and Darkness into Good
sections.summary: Closeness to Hashem makes it possible to discern the hidden good within painful and difficult realities.

sections.title: Creation, Divine Peace, and the Rectification of Evil
sections.summary: The sequence of creation and the sanctity of Shabbat culminate in the revelation of peace.

sections.title: Motzaei Shabbat and the Sixfold Language of Salvation
sections.summary: Verses recited around Havdalah carry the blessing of Shabbat into the coming six days.

topics.h: Six Expressions of Salvation at Havdalah

sections.title: Rosh Chodesh and the Renewal of Israel
sections.summary: The moon’s sanctification is linked to Israel’s special understanding of Torah and the rhythm of revelation.

wherein through the observance of Shabbat they are immediately redeemed,
ְּד ַׁש ָּב ת ְּב ָר ָז א ִּד ְב ִר ית ְּכ מֹו ֶׁש ָּכ תּוב ַּב ֹּזַה ר ַה ָּק דֹוׁש
for Shabbat is rooted in the mystery of the Covenant as written in the holy Zohar,
ְו ַה ְּז ַמ ן ְל ַת ֵּק ן ְּפ ָג ם ֶז ה ְו ִק ְל קּול ָאָד ם ָה ִר אׁשֹון
and it is the designated time to rectify this blemish and the fall of Adam the First,
ַמ ְז ִּכ יִר ין ֵא ִל ָּי הּו ַמ ְל ַא ְך ַה ְּב ִר ית
we mention Elijah, the angel of the Covenant;
ֶׁש ָּכ ל ֶנ ֶפ ׁש ִּב ְפ ָר ט ֶׁש ּזֹוֶכ ה ִל ְה יֹות ְמ ַׁש ֵּמ ר ַׁש ָּב ת ְּכ ִה ְל ָכ ָת ּה ִנ ְג ָאל ִמ ֹּכל ָו ֹכל
for every individual soul who merits to observe Shabbat according to its halakhot is redeemed completely,
ּוְמ ַב ְּק ִׁש ים ֶׁש ָּי ֹבא ֵא ִל ָּי הּו ִו יַב ֵּׂש ר ָל נּו ְּב ׂשֹורֹות טֹובֹות
and we beseech that Elijah come and announce unto us good tidings.
